questions.question: What are SQL joins and how do you use them in Rails?
questions.title: SQL Joins in Rails
questions.direct_answer: A JOIN combines rows from two tables on a related column. Types: INNER JOIN (rows that match in both), LEFT JOIN (all left rows; NULLs where right doesn't match), RIGHT/FULL (less common). In Rails: `User.joins(:posts)` produces an INNER JOIN (`JOIN posts ON posts.user_id = users.id`); `User.left_joins(:posts)` is a LEFT JOIN. Use joins when you want to FILTER by an association (users who have published posts: `User.joins(:posts).where(posts: {published: true})`) — it doesn't load the posts, just filters users. To load the associated records too, use `includes` (+ references) or `eager_load`. `joins` with a string is raw SQL: `joins('LEFT JOIN posts ON posts.user_id = users.id')`. Common gotcha: `joins(:posts)` returns users possibly duplicated (once per post); use `distinct` (`User.joins(:posts).distinct`) for unique users. Know the join types and that joins filters, includes loads.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know joins (INNER/LEFT) filter by an association, and that joins doesn't load the association (use includes/eager_load to load).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Expecting joins(:posts) to load posts (it only filters; use includes/eager_load to load them).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: joins(:posts) = INNER JOIN (filter by association); left_joins = LEFT JOIN. joins filters, includes/eager_load loads. Use distinct to dedupe.

sections.title: Combine Related Rows
sections.content: A JOIN combines rows from two tables on a related column. Types: INNER JOIN (rows that match in both), LEFT JOIN (all left rows; NULLs where right doesn't match), RIGHT or FULL (less common). In Rails: User joins posts produces an INNER JOIN (JOIN posts ON posts user id equals users id); User left joins posts is a LEFT JOIN. Use joins when you want to FILTER by an association (users who have published posts: User joins posts where posts published true) — it doesn't load the posts, just filters users. To load the associated records too, use includes (plus references) or eager load. joins with a string is raw SQL: joins LEFT JOIN posts ON posts user id equals users id. Common gotcha: joins posts returns users possibly duplicated (once per post); use distinct (User joins posts distinct) for unique users. Know the join types and that joins filters, includes loads.

sections.title: SQL Joins
sections.content:
INNER/LEFT JOIN combine rows on a related column. joins(:a) filters; includes/eager_load loads. distinct dedupes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[users] -- INNER JOIN --> P[posts]
  P --> M[matching rows only]
  LJ[left_joins] --> A[all users; NULL if no post]
  F[filter by assoc] --> J[joins]
  L[load assoc] --> I[includes/eager_load]
```

sections.title: SQL joins
sections.content:
```ruby
# JOIN types:
#   INNER JOIN  -> rows that match in BOTH tables
#   LEFT JOIN  -> all left rows; NULLs where right doesn't match
#   (RIGHT / FULL JOIN -> less common; some adapters)

# Rails: `joins` = INNER JOIN (FILTERS by association; doesn't load it)
User.joins(:posts)                    # JOIN posts ON posts.user_id = users.id
# -> users who have at least one post (posts NOT loaded)
User.joins(:posts).where(posts: { published: true })
# -> users who have a published post (still no posts loaded)

# `left_joins` = LEFT JOIN (all users; NULL where no post)
User.left_joins(:posts)

# To LOAD the associated records (not just filter), use includes/eager_load:
User.includes(:posts).where(posts: { published: true }).references(:posts)
User.eager_load(:posts)                # a JOIN that also loads posts

# String join (raw SQL):
User.joins('LEFT JOIN posts ON posts.user_id = users.id')
User.joins('INNER JOIN orders ON orders.user_id = users.id AND orders.paid = true')

# Multi-level joins:
User.joins(posts: :comments)           # users -> posts -> comments
User.joins(posts: [{ comments: :author }])

# Gotcha: joins(:posts) can DUPLICATE users (one row per post):
User.joins(:posts).count              # counts user-post pairs, not users
User.joins(:posts).distinct.count      # unique users who have posts
User.joins(:posts).distinct           # => distinct users

# Summary: joins FILTERS by association; includes/eager_load LOADS it; distinct dedupes.
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Expecting joins(:posts) to load posts (it only filters; use includes/eager_load to load).
Forgetting distinct after joins(:posts) (duplicate parents, one per child).
Mixing up INNER vs LEFT (INNER drops no-match rows; LEFT keeps them with NULLs).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: A JOIN combines rows from two tables on a related column (INNER = both match; LEFT = all left).
User.joins(:posts) = INNER JOIN — filters users by association; does NOT load posts.
User.left_joins(:posts) = LEFT JOIN (all users; NULLs where no post).
To LOAD the association, use includes (+ references) or eager_load, not joins.
joins(:posts) can duplicate users (one per post) — use distinct for unique users.
